history.dynasty: 13th century (Yadava period; ~800 years per local tradition) with multiple later renovations
history.period: Ancient site (Markandeya Purana: Jamadagni's tapobhumi; ancient name Bhingri); present temple ~13th century with later additions
history.summary: The Renuka Devi Temple at Renapur (taluka town, Latur district) is the gramdevata shrine of Renapur — the town's very name derives from Renuka Devi, and local legend says sage Jamadagni did penance here when the place was called Bhingri in the Dandakaranya region. Tradition holds that Parashurama worshipped his mother Renuka here and founded a temple that was later destroyed; about 800 years ago devotees, guided by a divine dream, recovered the goddess's tandla-form idol from the Rena river and re-consecrated it where the temple now stands. Architecturally the walled precinct has two ~20-ft ancient deepmalas at the entrance, including the famous 'shaking deepmala' (halnari/halti deepmala) — a 12th-century dry-stone structure with no lime between stones, engineered to flex and absorb tremors — plus mandap, sabhamandap, antaral in Hemadpanti stonework, and a garbhagriha with a four-tiered shikhara crowned by lion sculptures. CSV CLARIFICATION (checked per brief): this is NOT the Mahur Renuka Shakti Peetha — that famous temple is at Mahur, Nanded district. The Renapur temple is regarded as the pratirup (replica) of Mahur's Renuka, and the custom is to take darshan here before proceeding to Mahurgad. The documented Renapur temple is the correct Latur-district referent for this CSV row; CSV town corrected from 'Latur' to 'Renapur'.

name: Renuka Devi Temple
town_description: Renapur is a taluka town in Latur district, Maharashtra, about 14 km from Latur city; its name derives from Renuka Devi, the town's gramdevata and the aradhya deity of devotees across the district. Local lore calls it Jamadagni's ancient tapobhumi (then named Bhingri) and holds a saying that places Renapur's antiquity even before Pandharpur.

travel.airport: Latur Airport is the nearest (verify commercial flight availability).
travel.railway: Latur Railway Station is the nearest major railhead, approx. 14 km south.
travel.road: The temple is in central Renapur, 700 m from the Renapur bus stand; ST buses run to Renapur from towns across Latur district, and private vehicles can reach the temple parking.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sharadiya Navratri (ending in the Vijayadashami palkhi) and the Vaishakh Purnima three-day yatra are the grandest times.
